lessons.title: I have
lessons.objective: I have / I am [age] years old

lessons.title: I like / I love

lessons.title: I want to
lessons.explanation:

Tengo que + [infinitive]
This single pattern turns every verb you know into an obligation sentence.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Tengo que + [infinitive].

items.note: This single pattern turns every verb you know into an obligation sentence.

passage.target: Tengo que operar a las siete.
passage.native: I have to perform surgery at seven.

lessons.title: Going to · 3
lessons.explanation:
Voy a + [infinitive]
The near-future tense — simpler than the future conjugation and used far more in everyday speech.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Voy a + [infinitive].

items.native: What are you going to do after?
items.note: The near-future tense — simpler than the future conjugation and used far more in everyday speech.

passage.native: I'm going to explain the procedure.

passage.target: Vamos a llegar a las tres.
passage.native: We're going to arrive at three.
What are you going to do after?
